title: Shadow traffic petri-dish: replay + micro-synthesis log
content:
Purpose:
Run small-scale shadow traffic + synthetic micro-synth patterns to reproduce odd p99 spikes seen in canary on 2025-10-28. Quick, iterative notebook-style notes so I can hand off to SRE if needed.

Environment:
- cluster: dev-gpu-pool-6 (mixed A100/RTX6000), region: us-west1
- runtime build: serving-runtime@main (PR 2718 applied local patch for batch timeout)
- model: llama2-13b-quant-v2 (int8 runtime profile)
- traffic tool: ripsaw-replay (local fork) + synthetic-surge v0.3
- metric sink: local-prometheus (scrape 5s), jaeger sampling=0.1

Test plan (4 mini-cases):
A) steady steady: 200 qps constant for 10m (baseline)
B) micro-surge: add 50 qps pulses for 10s every 60s (10 pulses)
C) shadow-replay: replay production trace 30m @ scaled 0.1 (bursty clusters)
D) cold-shadow: same as C but clear KV cache before each 5m window

Commands (local):
- start metrics: ./infra/local_prom.sh up
- run steady: ./tools/ripsaw --qps 200 --dur 600 --model llama2-13b --out /tmp/runA.json
- micro-surge: ./tools/synth --pattern pulse --base 200 --pulse 50 --pulse-len 10 --period 60 --dur 600
- replay: ./tools/replay --trace traces/prod_slice_20251028.json --scale 0.1 --dur 1800

Quick raw observations (prom stats aggregated at 5s):
- Run A (steady): p50 18ms, p95 54ms, p99 128ms, max 352ms, throughput stable 198-202 qps. KV cache hit ~ 94%.
- Run B (micro-surge pulses): during pulses p50 jumps to 22ms, p95 89ms, p99 310-620ms (3 distinct spikes). Not every pulse spikes. Spike pattern: 2/10 pulses with >500ms p99.
- Run C (replay): periods of clustered arrivals produced frequent p99 spikes ~300-800ms and occasional 1.2s outliers. Observed long-tail correlated with enqueue backlog in worker q (queue_length metric).
- Run D (cold-shadow): clearing KV cache before windows increased p50 to 34ms baseline and p99 often >900ms during clusters. Suggests KV priming matters for these arrival patterns.

Interesting traces / root-cause leads:
- Trace samples from p99 during pulse show heavy time in "kv_cache_fetch" and "batch-assemble" spans. Some spans show retries/reschedule (worker preemption?)
- CPU on host spikes correspond to periods with long batch-assemble time; suspect a serialization hotspot in batch assembly under mem pressure.
- GPU utilization stays ~65-85% and does not saturate during spikes — points to CPU-side bottleneck (assembly + KV fetch)

Mini visual (ASCII sparkline of p99 across runB pulses - pulse index 1..10):
[ 1:130 ] [ 2:610* ] [ 3:140 ] [ 4:320 ] [ 5:150 ] [ 6:680* ] [ 7:160 ] [ 8:180 ] [ 9:140 ] [ 10:170 ]
(* = large spike)

Hypotheses:
- H1: KV cache eviction/partial misses during bursts cause synchronous fetches that block batch assembly and stall worker threads.
- H2: Batch assembly code serializes on a mutex under certain queue lengths leading to head-of-line blocking.
- H3: Prioritization/backpressure not applied early enough; short pulses push many small requests into same batch and assembly time increases superlinearly.

Quick experiments to validate (next runs):
1) Instrument: add timing for kv_cache_fetch per-request and batch-assemble lock hold time (simple micro-timers).
2) Run micro-surge with varied base qps (150 / 250) to see nonlinearity point.
3) Add randomized small jitter to request arrival in replay to avoid perfect alignment (does it reduce glaze spikes?).
4) Try optimistic prefetch for likely KV entries for warm paths (cheap, in-process cache) and measure delta.

TODOs / notes to self:
- Save top 10 p99 traces (trace ids list written to /tmp/high_p99_ids.txt) — done: /tmp/high_p99_ids.txt
- Open ticket to profile batch-assemble mutex (PRF-1197) and link traces.
- Ask SRE to run similar test on dedicated-pool-2 (more homogeneous GPU) to rule out mixed-host effects.
- Sketch a defensive quick-fix: limit batch size under high queue length or fallback to smaller-worker pool to reduce assembly stall time.

Conclusions (quick):
- Not a pure GPU limit. Evidence points to CPU-side batch assembly + KV cache priming being big contributors to p99 spikes in bursty traffic.
- Cold cache drastically increases risk; if product traffic includes short-lived cold paths, SLA risk goes up.

Notes for handoff:
- Relevant artifacts: /tmp/runB_metrics_20260118.prom.lz4, /tmp/high_p99_ids.txt, git branch "diag/shadow-petri-omar" in my fork.
- Recommended next owner: Maya (she owns batch assembly work) + SRE on-call for flaky infra runs.

Open questions: 
- Why do only some pulses spike? Are there interleaving system cron jobs (backup, snapshot) that align with minute boundaries? Check node-level cron logs for the test window.
- Could garbage collector pauses (python/worker) be co-occurring? Need GC metrics from workers.

Bottom line: follow-up instrument + rerun with prefetch and jitter. If assembly mutex holds found, we should patch quickly and run canary.

---END---
